chunks: As for your saying: Is it all due to the dislike of death?
Then by Allah, I do not care whether I enter into death or death comes out to me.
And as for your saying: Doubt regarding the people of Syria!
Then by Allah, I did not delay war for a day except that I hoped a group would join me, find guidance through me, and see my light with their weak eyes,
This is dearer to me than to kill them in their misguidance, although they would be bearing their own sins.
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali delay the battle at Siffin according to his explanation to his companions?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies that his delay at Siffin was not born of fear of death or doubt regarding the Syrians, but rather a strategic hope that a faction might join him to find guidance. He expresses that guiding them is preferable to fighting them while they remain in error, even if they bear the burden of their own sins. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of his patience as a deliberate choice for the sake of da'wah rather than a sign of weakness.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Well, as for your idea whether this (delay) is due to my unwillingness for death,
then by Allāh I do not care whether I proceed towards death or death advances towards me.
As for your impression that it may be due to my misgivings about the people of Syria (ash-Shām),
well, by Allāh, I did not put off war even for a day except in the hope that some group may join me, find guidance through me and see my light with their weak eyes.
This is dearer to me than to kill them in the state of their misguidance although they would be bearing their own sins.
